items.question: What is included in the monthly mortgage result?
items.answer: Principal and interest repay the loan. The modeled monthly total can also include the property tax, insurance, HOA and other costs you enter. Compare both figures before treating a payment as your housing budget; the formula section explains the fixed-rate loan calculation.

items.question: Where do I enter extra mortgage principal payments?
items.answer: Open Extra payments & dates for recurring monthly or annual extra principal, a one-time payment, or dated extra payments. Recalculate and review payoff timing, interest saved and the complete schedule. For a current balance and known regular payment, use the dedicated Mortgage Payoff tool.

items.question: Which tool should I use for a car, personal loan or mortgage?
items.answer: This page handles general loan mathematics. Auto Loan includes purchase-price and trade-in inputs; Personal Loan includes entered borrowing fees; Mortgage separates loan payments from entered ownership costs. Choose the tool whose inputs match the transaction.

items.question: How can I compare extra loan payments with the original schedule?
items.answer: Use Loan Repayment with the current principal, interest rate and regular payment, then add monthly, yearly or one-time extra payments. It compares payoff time and interest under fixed assumptions. After calculating a schedule, Download CSV provides data rows for a spreadsheet, rather than a workbook with formulas.

queries: compound interest calculator with monthly contributions
compound interest calculator with annual contributions
compound interest calculator - daily monthly yearly compounding
items.question: How do deposits and compounding frequency affect compound growth?
items.answer: Monthly and annual contributions are separate cash streams. Choose when deposits occur and the compounding frequency for the nominal rate you enter. Daily compounding does not mean a daily deposit; changing the frequency while holding a nominal rate fixed can change the ending balance.

queries: compound interest calculator with increasing contributions
items.question: How do I model deposits that increase each year?
items.answer: Use Savings when you need a yearly percentage increase in monthly or annual deposits. Compound Growth on this page uses constant deposit amounts. Keep the same starting balance, return and timing when comparing the two scenarios.

items.question: Should I project my savings or solve for a savings goal?
items.answer: Savings Interest projects a balance from the deposits you enter. Monthly Deposit Needed solves for a target amount and deadline; Time Needed solves for the first whole month reaching a target. Retirement planning adds a separate withdrawal horizon and retirement-income assumptions.

links.label: Find the monthly deposit for a goal
Find time to a savings goal

items.question: How should I use a quoted APY in a savings projection?
items.answer: APY is an effective annual yield, while a nominal interest rate also needs a compounding convention. For an effective annual rate, use the annual-compounding convention or first convert the quote with Equivalent Interest Rate. Enter only a rate you have checked; this site does not fetch current bank offers.

queries: mortgage payoff calculator from current balance
mortgage payoff calculator using current balance
mortgage payoff calculator based on remaining balance
items.question: Can I start with my current mortgage balance?
items.answer: Yes. Select Current balance and enter the remaining principal and current monthly principal-and-interest payment. Keep escrow costs separate from the loan payment. Original loan uses the original amount, term and elapsed payments to estimate the remaining position instead.

links.label: Start from a current mortgage balance

items.replacesQuestion: Should I enter my original mortgage or remaining balance?

queries: mortgage payoff calculator with biweekly and extra payments
mortgage payoff calculator with lump sum and extra payments
mortgage payoff calculator with extra principal payments
items.question: How do lump sums and biweekly payments change payoff?
items.answer: Choose the appropriate payment strategy and enter additional principal in the fields provided. A one-time extra payment is different from repeating the same amount every month. Compare the resulting schedule and interest with the baseline, and check your lender’s actual posting and prepayment rules.

queries: amortization calculator with extra principal payments
amortization calculator with taxes and insurance
items.question: Does an amortization schedule include extra principal and housing costs?
items.answer: Extra principal reduces the loan balance and can shorten the schedule. Property tax and insurance are housing costs, rather than principal repayment. Use the Mortgage calculation when you need those entered costs alongside the payment; use each schedule’s CSV for its complete rows.

queries: refinance calculator with taxes and insurance
items.question: How do cash-out and closing costs affect a refinance comparison?
items.answer: Cash-out increases the amount borrowed, and financed closing costs also become part of the new principal. Enter fees and points explicitly. The payment comparison is not a complete housing-cost budget; use Mortgage for a separate projection including entered taxes and insurance.

links.label: Compare a refinance from the current balance

items.replacesQuestion: How do financed refinance costs affect the loan?

items.question: Why are HELOC draw-period and repayment-period payments different?
items.answer: The draw period models interest-only payments on the entered initial advance; the repayment phase amortizes that balance. This is a constant-rate illustration with no additional draws, not a forecast of a lender’s variable rate or a general extra-payment plan.
items.replacesQuestion: Why can my HELOC payment rise after the draw period?

queries: heloc calculator how much can i borrow
items.question: How is the maximum HELOC credit estimate calculated?
items.answer: Maximum Credit starts with the home value, existing mortgage balance and combined loan-to-value limit you enter. The resulting equity capacity is not a lender approval and does not incorporate a credit score, appraisal decision or lender-specific eligibility rules.
items.replacesQuestion: How much home equity can I borrow against?

queries: home equity loan calculator monthly payment
home equity loan calculator fixed rate
items.question: How is a home equity loan different from this site’s HELOC model?
items.answer: This tool models an amortizing loan with a fixed entered rate and closing-cost treatment. HELOC instead separates a modeled interest-only draw period from repayment. The borrowing-capacity estimate is available in the HELOC tool, rather than inferred from the home equity loan payment.

links.label: Estimate a home equity loan payment

items.replacesQuestion: How is a home equity loan different from a HELOC?

items.question: Should I enter APY or a nominal interest rate for a CD?
items.answer: Use the compounding convention that matches your quote. A nominal rate compounded monthly differs from an effective annual APY. Equivalent Interest Rate can translate between those conventions; the CD tool then estimates maturity and the entered tax on positive interest, without fetching current offers.
items.replacesQuestion: Should I enter a CD's nominal rate or APY?

items.question: How can I calculate CAGR over a period stated in months?
items.answer: Convert months to years for the length-based form: 18 months is 1.5 years. Use Dates when you have exact endpoints. CAGR summarizes growth between two values and does not measure stock volatility or determine a future market return.

items.question: Can CAGR be converted directly into a return with contributions?
items.answer: Not from CAGR alone. Money added or withdrawn between endpoints requires the amounts and timing of those cash flows. Average Return’s Dated Cash Flows mode can estimate a money-weighted annual return when you supply those transactions; it does not convert a CAGR number into XIRR.

items.question: Which investment assumptions should I compare over time?
items.answer: Start with the same principal, deposit timing and time horizon, then vary the return assumption separately from contributions. The growth forms do not combine arbitrary deposits and withdrawals. Use Retirement for its supported retirement saving and withdrawal scenarios; expected returns remain assumptions.

queries: future value calculator with monthly contributions
items.question: How do I use monthly contributions in Future Value?
items.answer: Enter the number of monthly periods and a rate per month, with the periodic contribution and its beginning- or end-of-period timing. Do not enter an annual rate as a monthly rate. Compound Interest is a convenient alternative when your inputs are an annual quote and years plus months.
items.replacesQuestion: How do I calculate future value with regular deposits?

items.question: How can I compare a future amount with today’s purchasing power?
items.answer: First calculate the future balance under your return and payment assumptions. Then adjust that amount using an explicit inflation rate or compare with Real Return. This separates nominal growth from purchasing power; it does not add an inflation field or withdrawal stream to this periodic-value form.

links.label: Adjust an amount back to today

queries: present value calculator for monthly payments
present value calculator with discount rate
items.question: How do I discount a stream of monthly payments?
items.answer: Use the annuity mode with a monthly rate and number of months. Keep payment timing consistent, and include any separate future amount only once. Pension compares entered lump-sum and pension offers with life-expectancy and COLA assumptions; it does not calculate a government pension entitlement.

items.question: Which return calculator fits a rental property investment?
items.answer: ROI compares the cost and proceeds you enter, while Rental Property models rents, vacancy, expenses, financing and a sale assumption over a holding period. For transactions on individually chosen dates, use Dated Cash Flows. Do not treat these different return conventions as interchangeable.

items.question: When should I compare arithmetic and geometric average returns?
items.answer: Arithmetic average describes the mean periodic return; geometric average reflects compounded growth across the entered periods. Enter the returns you have, including losses and zero-return periods. The tool does not retrieve stock, index or fund histories, and does not calculate a portfolio-weighted average from holdings.

items.question: How can I compare fund and advisor fees over time?
items.answer: Compare A and B using the same balance, contributions and return basis. Fund fees and advisor fees affect both amounts paid and later growth, so the ending-balance difference is not simply total fees paid. Enter the actual percentages yourself; the tool does not look up a provider’s price schedule.

items.question: How do lump sums and recurring deposits affect this fund projection?
items.answer: Use starting principal for a lump sum and the monthly or annual contribution fields for recurring deposits. Enter the return and fee assumptions rather than a fund ticker. This is a generic projection, not a fund recommendation, live NAV lookup or a country-specific SIP tax calculation.

queries: payback period calculator irregular cash flows
payback period calculator no discount rate
items.question: How do unequal cash flows and a discount rate affect payback?
items.answer: Irregular Cash Flow accepts one net cash flow per year, preserving zero years and additional investments. Ordinary payback accumulates the entered flows; discounted payback first adjusts them for the discount rate. A zero discount rate removes that discounting assumption.

links.label: Use a repeating annual cash flow

items.replacesQuestion: How is discounted payback different from simple payback?

items.question: How are bond price and yield related in this model?
items.answer: Price discounts coupon and face-value payments using the entered yield and frequency; Yield solves the reverse relationship from a price. Dated Bond uses settlement, maturity and the selected day-count convention. Savings-bond redemption rules and market quotes are not supplied.

items.question: How do nominal return and inflation combine?
items.answer: Real return uses (1 + nominal return) / (1 + inflation) − 1 for a matching period. The value mode also shows modeled purchasing power under the entered tax and time assumptions. Supply the nominal return yourself; stock and fund history is not retrieved.
items.replacesQuestion: Why not simply subtract inflation from return?

queries: simple interest calculator for savings account
items.question: How do I calculate simple interest for days or months?
items.answer: Choose the rate period and time unit explicitly. Simple interest applies the rate to the original principal; it does not compound interest or build an amortizing payment schedule. For two calendar dates, first obtain the elapsed days from Date Calculator and check the lender’s day-count convention.

links.label: Set the rate and time units

items.question: Can I review the rental property projection in a spreadsheet?
items.answer: After calculating, open Calculation details and use Download CSV for the complete modeled schedule. CSV contains data rows, not a spreadsheet template with live formulas. Keep the entered vacancy, expense growth and sale assumptions with the export when comparing properties.

queries: rent calculator based on yearly income
items.question: How do I calculate a rent budget from annual or monthly income?
items.answer: Choose the income frequency and enter non-housing debt separately. The housing and total-debt ratios are planning assumptions you can change. This estimates an affordability budget, not a landlord’s asking rent, a roommate split or a location-specific rental requirement.

items.question: How should I choose an emergency-fund target?
items.answer: Multiply essential monthly expenses by the number of months you choose, then compare with existing emergency savings. Savings Plan estimates months of deposits needed at the entered contribution. This is an expense-based planning target, without a country-specific benefit or insurance model.
items.replacesQuestion: How much should I have in an emergency fund?

items.question: How can I estimate future college costs and a savings gap?
items.answer: Enter today’s annual cost, cost growth, attendance duration and time until enrollment, then compare the funding need with existing savings and assumed investment growth. Costs by school and 529-specific deductions, contribution limits and eligibility are not retrieved or calculated.

links.label: Plan from an entered college cost

queries: retirement calculator with pension and social security
items.question: How can I include pension or Social Security income in a retirement target?
items.answer: Required Savings has an Other monthly retirement income input for an amount you already know. Use an estimate appropriate to the scenario; this does not build a pension entitlement, coordinate a couple’s Social Security benefits or import a benefit statement.

queries: retirement calculator how long will my money last
items.question: Where can I estimate how long a retirement balance lasts?
items.answer: Savings Longevity uses the starting balance, fixed monthly withdrawal and return you enter. It is a different question from solving a monthly saving target or a retirement-age balance. Compare several return and spending assumptions rather than reading the result as a guaranteed depletion date.

queries: auto loan calculator with taxes and fees
auto loan calculator with trade in
items.question: How do trade-in credit, negative equity and purchase taxes enter an auto loan?
items.answer: Enter the trade-in value and amount still owed separately: positive equity reduces financing, while an unpaid balance can increase it. Use the documented dealer-purchase tax treatment for a supported state or select Manual and enter assumptions. This does not quote an APR from a credit score or resolve every local tax rule.
items.replacesQuestion: How does negative trade-in equity affect my car loan?

queries: auto loan calculator with extra payments
auto loan calculator with extra payments and lump sum
items.question: Can this purchase calculator compare extra repayments?
items.answer: The purchase form determines a regular payment or affordable vehicle price; it has no independent extra-payment comparison. Once you know the actual balance, annual interest rate and regular payment, Loan Repayment can compare additional principal under its own fixed-rate assumptions.

queries: down payment calculator for first-time home buyer
items.question: Does the cash-needed result include closing costs?
items.answer: Cash Needed combines the selected down payment with the closing costs you enter. It does not automatically itemize lender and title charges or determine first-time-buyer assistance eligibility. Home Price and Down Payment Percentage solve different unknowns from the same entered cash budget.
items.replacesQuestion: Are closing costs part of the down payment?

items.question: Does a debt-to-income result establish loan approval?
items.answer: No. The ratio compares the monthly debts and gross monthly income you enter. Lenders also consider credit, assets, documented income and product-specific rules. House Affordability adds entered housing costs and planning ratios to estimate a price budget.
